conversation: The chain-of-thought reasoning section is what separates toy demos from production-grade agentic systems. One nuance worth adding: in multi-agent workflows, chain-of-thought becomes even more critical because you need each agent to expose its reasoning to the orchestration layer so the next agent in the pipeline can verify it rather than blindly trusting it. In practice this means the orchestrator doesn't just pass data between agents - it validates the reasoning chain at each handoff boundary. We've found this catches about 80% of hallucination-driven cascade failures before they propagate downstream. The cost implication is real though - chain-of-thought tokens are expensive. A practical pattern: use a cheap classifier model to decide whether the current step needs full chain-of-thought reasoning or can proceed with direct output, then only invoke the expensive reasoning path when confidence is below threshold. This keeps the quality high while cutting reasoning token costs by roughly half.
